Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second chapter to unfold. The umpires are on their way toward the pitch, and the fielders of Ireland have scattered to take their respective positions. Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan will open for Bangladesh. Matthew Humphreys will start with the new ball. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 171 is what Bangladesh need to win and level the series. The pitch does look excellent for batting, even though a few of the deliveries seem to be holding in the pitch and we should see even more dew in the second half of the game. Can the Irish bowlers do the job upfront just like they did in the first T20I? Or will the hosts manage to get over the line? Only time will tell. The run chase is up next, stay tuned.

Mahedi Hasan is up for a chat. He says that he focused on keeping the basics right, maintaining tight lines and lengths after the powerplay, which contributed to his success today. He ended up saying that he is confident that his team's batting ability to chase down the target.

Bangladesh made multiple changes on the back of that defeat in the first game but the change in personnel didn't bear any fruit, at least not early on. Mahedi Hasan and Nasum Ahmed conceded a total of 27 runs in the first 2 overs, setting the tone for the rest of the Powerplay and Mohammad Saifuddin's first over went for 16 as well. They were staring down the barrel of a 200-run plus total but did brilliantly in the middle overs to pull things back. Mahedi Hasan led the fightback and Tazim Hasan Sakib also bowled really well but Saifuddin and even Mustafizur Rahman were off colour.

Ireland were riding high on confidence from the first T20I win and it immediately showed when they came out to bat. Skipper Paul Stirling and the in-form Tim Tector went berserk inside the Powerplay and even though Stirling got out, Ireland scored 75 runs in the first 6 overs. They did slow down in the middle overs as they kept losing wickets but it was a decent finish at the death, thanks to Lorcan Tucker who hung around till the end and remained unbeaten on 41.

End of a high-octane and probably lengthy first half (thanks to the floodlight failure early on) of the game that saw the tide turn in both teams' favour. However, at the end of the first 20 overs, Ireland will still feel that the total of 170 on the board is a really good one, but will also feel that it could have easily been a lot more.

OUT! RUN OUT! Mustafizur Rahman dishes a bouncer, outside off. Gareth Delany attempts to pull but this time the ball beats the outside edge. Lorcan Tucker started sprinting toward the striker's end as soon as the ball was delivered. But Litton Das gloves the ball, runs toward the stumps and underarms it to the wicket directly. Ireland have scored 170 runs on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: A fourth leg bye in the over! Bowls it a bit fuller and straighter, the ball nips back in and beats Paul Stirling completely before crashing into the pads. There's an appeal for LBW but it is turned down and that seemed to be missing leg stump.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, this time straighter and angled into the pads. Stirling fails to flick it away and the ball goes off the pads behind square leg. Just a leg bye then.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that did so much off the deck! Full of a good length and around off, the ball nips back in a mile and Stirling is caught off guard. The ball clips the back thigh pad and goes through to the keeper. There's a stifled appeal but nothing more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Tanzim Hasan Sakib to Paul Stirling, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The Irish openers are out in the middle and so are the layers of Bangladesh. Paul Stirling and Tim Tector have walked out to open for the visitors with Mahedi Hasan ready to bowl the first over of the contest.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is pitchside. He says that the weather looks great for the second T20I and comments that the surface in the first T20I was good, particularly for batters. He mentions that Hridoy batted brilliantly, setting an example for the other batters on how to bat on this surface. He also praises Humphreys' bowling, noting that his quick pace, with 21 out of 28 balls clocked over 100 kph, was effective. Ed provides details about the pitch and ground dimensions for today's match, mentioning that it's pitch No. 4 with a good covering of grass. He describes the ground's layout and boundary lengths, concluding that a score of 180-200 would be par.

Litton Das, the captain of Bangladesh, says that every game is a challenge and they are looking forward to it. Adds that the bowlers just need to bowl in the right areas and reckons that the pitch looks like a good one. Informs that they have made three changes with the likes of Nurul Hasan, Mohammad Saifuddin and Mahedi Hasan coming in.

Ireland captain Paul Stirling has informed that they'll be batting first after winning the toss and will be looking to replicate their successful approach from the first T20I. Stirling acknowledged areas for improvement, particularly in catching, and is confident they'll work on those in this game. Ireland has made one change to their lineup, with Ben Calitz replacing Curtis Campher.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Litton Das (C/WK), Saif Hassan, Tawhid Hridoy, Nurul Hasan, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Mahedi Hasan (In for Jaker Ali), Mohammad Saifuddin (In for Shoriful Islam), Mustafizur Rahman, and Nasum Ahmed (In for Rishad Hossain).

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Tim Tector, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Ben Calitz (replaces Curtis Campher), George Dockrell, Gareth Delany, Mark Adair, Barry McCarthy, Matthew Humphreys, Josh Little.
TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and they have decided to BAT first.

Can Bangladesh break their losing streak and level the series, or will Ireland continue their winning run and take an unassailable lead? The contest promises to be intense, with both teams looking to gain the upper hand. Get ready for a cracking game of T20 cricket. Toss and team updates in a bit.

Bangladesh will need to significantly improve in both bowling and batting performances if they are to level the series. Their top order was decimated in the first T20I, and Tawhid Hridoy was left with no support from the other end. Their batting order will be looking to provide some stability. Ireland, meanwhile, will be hoping to continue their strong bowling performance, with Matthew Humphreys and Mark Adair leading the charge with the ball and Harry Tector with the bat.

Ireland, on the other hand, is riding high on confidence after their convincing win in the first T20I. Led by Harry Tector's unbeaten 69, Ireland's batters showed they can take on Bangladesh's bowling, posting a competitive 181. Their bowlers, particularly Matthew Humphreys, who took a four-fer and Mark Adair, who picked up a couple, were equally impressive, restricting Bangladesh to 142. The side will be keen to seal the fate of the series with a game to spare by winning again.

Hello and welcome to the fans tuning in. The second T20I of the contest between Bangladesh and Ireland is set to be a cracker after what we witnessed in the first game. The home team, Bangladesh, is looking to bounce back from a thumping 39-run defeat in the series opener. The Litton Das-led side has been extremely strong at home, but a 0-3 loss to West Indies and the recent hammering by Ireland have raised concerns. They'll be looking to regroup and come out strong in this crucial encounter.

The three-match T20I series between Bangladesh and Ireland has burst into life, with the visitors delivering a stunning performance in the opener to take an unexpected 1-0 lead. All eyes now turn to the second T20I at the Bir Sreshtho Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman Stadium in Chattogram, where Bangladesh will fight to level the series and Ireland will seek to create history with a series-clinching win. Ireland's victory in the first T20I was comprehensive, marking their first T20I win in 14 months and only their third ever against the Bangla Tigers. The home side is under immense pressure after a top-order capitulation. They have already secured the Test series, but a T20I series loss at home would be a significant blow, especially after their past success in this format against Ireland. Ireland enter the second T20I with massive confidence. They showcased an all-round performance that was clinical and highly disciplined, proving their potential in the shorter format. A win here would secure their first-ever T20I series victory against Bangladesh. Bangladesh are expected to bounce back, but Ireland's balanced attack and in-form batters pose a serious threat. This match will be a huge test of the home side's mental fortitude under pressure. Who are you backing for the win?
